title: Lesson 2. What CSS is and how to link it
description: Tags, the style.css file, the <link> tag, selectors, properties and style

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 2 — **CSS**: we'll learn to style a site and link a stylesheet. Two rooms and one door — you'll see what that means in a moment. Let's go!

slides.text: A **tag** is a command in HTML. It tells the browser what goes here: a heading, text, an image, a button. It's written in angle brackets `< >`.
Most tags are **paired**: an opening one and a closing one. The closing one has `/`. The text in between is what you see on screen.

Common tags: `

` … `

` — headings (h1 is the biggest) `

` — paragraph `` — link `` — image (no closing tag) `

check.prompt: Which of these tags is a closing tag?
The tag has a closing tag .
check.explain: is an exception: it has no closing tag.

slides.text: **CSS** is the language for how a page looks: color, size, font, layout. **HTML** says **what** is on the page, and **CSS** says **how** it looks (red, big, centered).
No door — HTML knows nothing about CSS, and the decorations don't work.

check.prompt: Match the part and its role

slides.text: Step 1. In VS Code open the project folder, click **New File** in the Explorer panel and name the file `style.css`. It must be in **the same folder** as index.html. No spaces or capital letters in the name.
Step 2. Put in the door — inside `<head>`:
`rel="stylesheet"` means «this is a stylesheet». `href="style.css"` is which file we connect to — where the door opens.
Check: write p { color: red; } in style.css, save it (Ctrl + S) and refresh the browser (F5). If the text is red, the door works.

check.prompt: Where does the <link> tag for CSS go?
«My Style.css» is a good name for a CSS file.
check.explain: No spaces or capital letters in the name: style.css.

slides.text: First we say **who** we style, then **how**. Today we call elements by their tag name:

`p` — the **selector**, who we style (all `

`) `{ }` — the styling goes inside `color` — the **property**, what we change `blue` — the **value**, what we make it `;` — at the end of each line

In a selector, the tag has no < >: p, not

. A colon goes between property and value. Every line ends with ; — forget it, and the next line may not work.

check.prompt: What is p called in the rule p { color: blue; }?
check.explain: The selector says who we style.
Tag without < >, a colon, a semicolon.

slides.text: `width` — width, `height` — height, `font-size` — letter size, `color` — text color. **px** (pixel) is the smallest dot on the screen. Colors can be written as a word (`red`) or a code (`#ff0000`).
To see that width and height work, add background-color. Without a background, you can't see the block's edges.

check.prompt: Which property changes the size of letters?

sections.title: All p at once and why style wins

slides.text: One rule for all: `p { color: blue; }` changes **all** paragraphs at once, however many there are. But the 5th one has its own style:
Result: all paragraphs are **blue**, and the 5th is **red**. The browser's rule: **a more precise and closer instruction wins**. style is written right in the tag and applies only to it.

The teacher told the whole class: «Write with a blue pen». Then told one student separately: «You write with a red one». That student follows the personal instruction, because it was said to them specifically.

check.prompt: A style attribute on one paragraph changes the color of all paragraphs.
check.explain: style affects only its own element.
